clues.text: This chief town sits on a big island in the far north of Canada. It is the largest town in its territory and the town farthest north in the land.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside far northern Canada and its large Arctic islands

source.quote: Located on Baffin Island, it is the territory's largest community and only city, and the northernmost city in Canada.

clues.text: It has a polar climate, even though it lies well south of the Arctic Circle. Cold deep sea water just off the island keeps the city cold.
clues.narrowing: rules out milder northern cities; the cold is driven by the nearby cold current, a paradox this far south of the Arctic Circle

source.quote: Iqaluit has a polar climate, influenced by the cold deep waters of the Labrador Current just off Baffin Island, which makes the city cold, although it is well south of the Arctic Circle.

clues.text: In 1999, this town was made the chief town of a brand new territory. The Northwest Territories had just split into two parts.
clues.narrowing: rules out capitals that were not created by the 1999 split of the Northwest Territories

source.quote: In 1999, Iqaluit was designated the capital of Nunavut after the division of the Northwest Territories into two separate territories.

clues.text: No roads or trains link this city to the rest of Canada. Ships can reach it for only part of the year, so goods from far away cost a lot.
clues.narrowing: rules out all but the roadless, ship-only-for-part-of-the-year northern capitals

source.quote: This is due to Iqaluit's isolation and heavy dependence on expensive imported supplies, as the city, like the rest of Nunavut, has no road or rail connections to the rest of Canada, and has ship connections for only part of the year.

clues.text: Of all the chief towns in Canada, this one has the least folks. No chief town in the land has so few folks.
clues.narrowing: converts: the lowest-population capital city in Canada

source.quote: Iqaluit has the lowest population of any capital city in Canada.
